svg.aria-label: How to write ஆனால்: 5 parts, ஆ, ன, ா, ல, ், one after another
svg.title: Writing ஆனால்
svg.desc: 5 parts written one after another: ஆ, ன, ா, ல, ் (tamil). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which is not always the order they are typed: a vowel sign written to the left of its consonant comes before it. Each vowel sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ஆ: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, ஆ (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ன: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 13, ன (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 195 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ா: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 36 (ா, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012) <https://lipitk.sourceforge.net/lipi-reco.htm>; ல: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 9, ல (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 194 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ்: Abhinaya Rajarajan, Varai (Swift Student Challenge 2026), reference drawings recorded by hand for the 18 Tamil consonants with pulli, க் to ன் (repository commit 952294fa, no licence: facts only) <https://github.com/abhinayaRajarajan/varai>. Source notes on variation: ஆ: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. This is one attested order. ன: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. Appendix I Frame 13 numbers six hand-movements for ன. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the six movements in order without lifting: the top bar runs out to the right edge, so the pen comes back along it to the right upright and draws the upright down. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 94% of the 335 stored prototypes of ன are a single pen-down stroke. ா: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 189 of the 217 stored prototypes of the aa sign (87%) are one pen-down stroke. In 135 of those 189 the pen starts on the left, partway down, and first moves down; 154 end at the foot of the right upright. So the left upright is drawn down, climbed back to the top bar, and the right upright comes last, without lifting. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline, whose top bar runs a little past the right upright. Handwriting varies by writer. ல: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. This is one attested order. ்: One writer's recorded reference drawings, stored in the order they were drawn. In all 18 the consonant body is one stroke and the puḷḷi is a separate second stroke, made after the body is complete, so it costs one pen lift. Its centre sits above the body at 0.47 to 0.65 of the body's width (0.54 for க்). An earlier reading of Info-farmer's Writing Tamil animations of the consonants on Wikimedia Commons, which show each consonant with its puḷḷi, also places the dot after the body. Confidence is medium: one recorded writer, and only stroke count, order and the dot's bounding box were read; the dot is about 10 by 13 canvas units, too small to say which way the pen moved, so the short downward dab drawn here is not a claim. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil disc, which the font centres at 0.43 to 0.60 of the consonant's width, a little left of where this writer put it. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 6 movements
Part 2 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Part 3 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 4 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, ஆ (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192
Part 2: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 13, ன (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 195
Part 3: stroke order after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 36 (ா, aa sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from
Part 4: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 9, ல (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 194
Part 5: stroke order after Abhinaya Rajarajan, Varai (Swift Student Challenge 2026), reference drawings recorded by hand for the 18 Tamil consonants with pulli, க் to ன் (repository
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
